title: Amazon Prime Video renews Kirk Herbstreit's contract with a clause.
seoTitle: Amazon Renews Kirk Herbstreit's Contract With a Clause
subtitle: The extension includes the possibility of replacing the analyst if a more attractive target emerges for the Thursday Night Football broadcast
excerpt: Amazon Prime Video extended Kirk Herbstreit's Thursday Night Football contract but kept a clause allowing them to terminate the deal if they can.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Amazon Prime Video has finalized a contract extension for Kirk Herbstreit to remain in the Thursday Night Football booth, but inserted a condition that allows them to terminate the agreement if a more attractive candidate for the role emerges.

Kirk Herbstreit's contract extension

According to Andrew Marchand of The Athletic, Amazon secured Herbstreit's continued presence on the Thursday Night Football broadcast beyond the 2026 season. The deal keeps the analyst on the team covering the NFL on Thursdays.

Flexibility clause for Amazon

The same source indicates that the contract includes the possibility for Amazon to terminate the agreement if it manages to hire another professional for the same role. This clause serves as leverage in negotiations with future targets.

Amazon's interest in Sean McVay

Reports indicate that Amazon considered Sean McVay, head coach of the Los Angeles Rams, as one of the top names to join the Thursday Night Football broadcast team. In 2022, following his Super Bowl victory, rumors emerged that McVay could receive a contract exceeding $15 million per year to transition to TV.

Financial offer for McVay

According to the same report, Amazon had reportedly prepared an offer of up to $100 million over five years if McVay accepted the invitation. The amount exceeds the annual salary he received as coach, estimated at $15 million.

Herbstreit's current situation and outlook

Herbstreit remains under contract with Amazon, but the agreement allows the broadcaster to take a year-by-year approach, keeping the door open for names like Travis Kelce, Troy Aikman, Greg Olsen, or others who do not divide their attention between college and professional football. Meanwhile, Herbstreit is still fulfilling his contract with ESPN, which is scheduled to end at the conclusion of the 2027 season.

With information from Bleacher Report, NBC Sports.
